_comment: Dasher v6 cross-platform capability matrix — THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Rendered at https://dasher.at/status/. How to update: https://dasher.at/developers/feature-parity/. Validated by scripts/validate-feature-status.mjs in CI. August 2026 audit: every row re-verified against the shipped code of each frontend; 'beta' on this pass often means 'implemented but not yet tested with real assistive hardware/users'.

meta.v5_baseline: Dasher v5 shipped native frontends for Windows, Linux/GTK, macOS and iOS (Android had a separate community project, acl33/AndroidDasher; Mac/iPhone were unmaintained by the 5.0 beta). Input covered mouse, stylus/tablet, touch, multitouch, tilt, joystick (Linux) and socket input — the UDP socket was the eye-tracker conduit, and Linux/Windows v5 also had direct-entry keyboard modes. Notable v5 features: game/training mode, eye-tracker autocalibration, PPM family language models, Kanji/Pinyin conversion, PDF screenshot export and three TTS backends (SAPI / speech-dispatcher / flite).

status_legend.beta: Available but untested / behind a flag / partial
status_legend.not-supported: Not available — usually a platform limitation

features.title: Pointer input (mouse / trackpad)
features.notes: The core steering model on every platform. On iOS/Android the pointer is driven by touch; on visionOS by native eye gaze.

features.title: Eye-gaze via system pointer handoff
features.notes: An eye tracker that controls the OS pointer drives Dasher — no tracker SDK involved, Dasher just consumes pointer events. Works today on any platform whose tracker moves the system cursor; not tested with real eye-gaze users yet outside Windows.

macos.reason: Works via pointer; no tracker integration, untested

visionos.reason: Native eye gaze is the system pointer

gtk.reason: Works via pointer; untested with trackers

ios.reason: No pointer handoff API at the time

features.title: Eye-gaze: raw tracker data (SDK / network)
features.notes: Dasher talks to the tracker directly — Tobii Stream Engine and eyetuitive/eye tribe SDKs, or a UDP gaze feed — with a tracker picker in Settings. Windows is currently the only frontend doing this. Linux and macOS are possibilities (need a socket-input path / tracker SDK); iOS cannot take raw data at all.

macos.reason: Outside chance — needs tracker SDK work

ios.reason: No raw tracker data access on iOS

windows.reason: Tobii Stream Engine, eyetuitive, UDP gaze + tracker picker

gtk.reason: Outside chance — needs socket/UDP input path

features.title: Direct touch input
features.notes: Touch drives the Dasher pointer. Touch is the primary input on Android and iOS. v5's multi-finger gestures (e.g. two-finger pause on iOS) are not yet ported to any v6 frontend.

features.title: Single / dual switch (button modes)
features.notes: The engine filters exist and each frontend wires them, but none have been tested with real switch users or switch hardware — treat all v6 entries as unvalidated. Apple: switchesOnly access method + 4 switch profiles with key capture and scan rate. Windows: 1/2-switch selection methods map to the engine filters. GTK: input filter selectable in Settings → Input; keys 1–4/F1–4/space fixed (no remapping UI). Scanning (auto-scan boxes) exists as an Apple selection method; also untested.

macos.reason: Wired (profiles, key capture); untested with hardware

features.title: Joystick / gamepad input
features.notes: GTK uses SDL3 (axes, buttons, haptics). Android reads gamepads via InputDevice motion events (shipped v0.1.x; not yet exercised with real controllers). Apple declares joystick in its access-method enum (macOS only) but has no backing service. Windows is on the backlog.

features.title: Tilt to steer (device tilt)
features.notes: iOS uses CoreMotion accelerometer with deadzone calibration. Android uses the game-rotation-vector sensor.

features.title: Socket / external cursor input
features.notes: The v5 conduit for eye trackers and external assistive apps (UDP coordinate protocol). Not re-implemented in v6 yet; Windows covers raw trackers via SDK feeds instead.

windows.reason: UDP gaze tracker covers part of this

features.title: Hand tracking
features.notes: visionOS drives the pointer natively from pinch + hand position.

macos.reason: Hand tracking APIs did not exist

ios.reason: Hand tracking APIs did not exist

features.title: Continuous (always moving)
features.notes: Dasher zooms continuously towards the cursor. The default experience on every platform.

features.title: Dwell to select
features.dasher_core_dep: Frontend dwell handler / engine dwell filter
features.notes: Hold the pointer still to click/select. GTK ships dwell-to-click (Preferences → Input) as a frontend feature; Apple exposes dwell as a selection method with an indicator; Windows is on the backlog.

features.title: Click / tap to zoom
features.notes: Each click advances the zoom one step (discrete control). Apple exposes pressToMove and clickToZoom selection methods; other frontends not yet.

features.title: Direct mode (tap boxes)
features.notes: The screen is divided into letter boxes that you tap directly. Apple implements this as a macOS selection method. Distinct from direct text entry (see Output).

features.title: Haptic / rumble feedback
features.notes: GTK uses SDL3 haptic/rumble for gamepad feedback. Android has a vibrator available but nothing is wired yet.

features.title: Dasher canvas rendering
features.notes: Every frontend renders the DasherCore command buffer natively (Metal/CoreGraphics, Avalonia, Cairo, Android Canvas).

features.title: Real font metrics for label layout
features.notes: The engine measures node labels with the frontend's actual font (DasherCore #56), fixing jumbled/overlapping letters at deep zoom — a v6 regression from v5's native metrics. Landed engine-side in v0.2.4; frontends adopt it one by one.

features.title: Colour palette selection
features.notes: DasherCore ships 22 colour palettes; every frontend exposes a picker (GTK with live swatches).

features.title: Custom font family & size
features.notes: Canvas glyph font family + size on every frontend (RFC 0016 work improved naming). Size range 8–72.

features.title: Left / right-handed layout
features.notes: Dasher renders left-to-right or right-to-left to suit handedness. Engine-provided, surfaced in each settings UI.

features.title: Dark mode / themes
features.notes: Appearance-aware palette switching (light/dark companions), shipped via RFC 0007.

features.title: Node-tree (custom) rendering
features.notes: A second rendering path exposing the live node tree for 3D / VR / custom views (RFC 0013). Engine API implemented and tested; no production frontend uses it yet. Future hope: a spatial eye-tracked port (e.g. Meta Quest).

macos.reason: Engine ready; experimental cube branch unmerged

features.title: PPM prediction (default model)
features.notes: Prediction by Partial Matching — the default language model, provided by DasherCore to every frontend.

features.title: Alternative models (Word / Mixture / CTW / KenLM)
features.notes: DasherCore registers 4 built-in language models (PPM, Word, Mixture, CTW). Android additionally integrates KenLM.

features.title: Adaptive learning (LM adapts as you type)
features.notes: The language model learns from entered text. Exposed as a toggle in each settings UI.

features.title: Alphabet & language selection
features.notes: v5 carried ~140 alphabet definitions; v6 expands to 622 via WorldAlphabets (9 curated + 486 autoConverted + 127 legacy), including native v5-format XML support.

features.title: Pinyin / CJK conversion
features.notes: DasherCore ships CJK alphabet files and a conversion system; carried over from v5. Real-world usage not yet validated in v6.

macos.reason: Engine support; untested with CJK users

features.title: Image labels for alphabet symbols
features.notes: Optional image= attribute on alphabet symbols (RFC 0014). Engine + macOS frontend ready; no bundled alphabet uses images yet.

macos.reason: Engine + frontend ready; no alphabet ships images

features.title: Spoken output (text-to-speech)
features.notes: Apple: swift-tts-wrapper (21 engines). Windows: DotNetTtsWrapper (SAPI + cloud). GTK: rust-tts-wrapper — speech-dispatcher on from-source Linux builds, cloud engines in the Flatpak/AppImage. Android: system TextToSpeech with speak-last-word toggle.

features.title: Speak typed text on stop
features.notes: Reads accumulated text aloud when Dasher stops. Apple Speech settings; Android speaks word-by-word while typing (speak-all-on-stop not wired); GTK speaks per word via the Speech toggle.

features.title: Copy text to clipboard
features.notes: Copy / Copy All on every frontend; Android adds a share sheet.

features.title: Paste / insert text
features.notes: Paste clipboard contents into Dasher's buffer (used to re-train context from existing text).

features.title: System-wide direct text entry (keyboard mode)
features.notes: Dasher becomes an on-screen keyboard: canvas-only window, output injected into the focused app. Windows: SendInput + non-activating topmost window. macOS: Accessibility API (CGEvent). GTK: ydotool/uinput with daemon probing + failure surfacing (v0.2.6+). Android: IME service. Contract: governance RFC 0015. Known gap: Windows doesn't forward deletes yet (Dasher-Windows #26).

features.title: Save / open files
features.notes: Save the buffer and re-open text files. Android uses the system save/share pickers.

features.title: Undo / redo typed text
features.notes: Undo/redo of typed text. Not implemented on any v6 frontend yet (the engine supports the edit operations).

features.title: PDF / screenshot export
features.notes: Export the Dasher canvas as a PDF/screenshot. A v5 GTK feature not yet ported to any v6 frontend (an earlier revision of this matrix claimed an F8 shortcut in v6 GTK — that did not exist).

features.title: Control mode (edit via Dasher nodes)
features.notes: Special nodes in the zooming interface for text-editing actions (select all, copy, move cursor, delete, speak…). Windows is the first v6 frontend to wire it; Android follows; v5 had it everywhere.

features.title: Typing rate display (WPM / CPS)
features.notes: Live typing speed over a rolling window, computed engine-side (RFC 0012). Apple and Windows show WPM/max/avg; GTK shows CPS+WPM in Settings → Output with reset.

features.title: App version shown in Settings
features.notes: The app reports its version in Settings → Privacy so support conversations can identify the build (RFC 0016). Tag-driven: Android derives it from the git tag (v0.1.9+); GTK derives from git describe (PR pending).

features.title: Grouped settings UI (by usage context)
features.notes: Settings grouped per the engine manifest (Customization/Input/Language/Output/Game Mode…). See dasher-design-guide for the normative structure.

features.title: Auto-discover engine parameters
features.notes: Settings UI generated from the engine's parameter schema at runtime, so new engine parameters appear without frontend changes.

features.title: Save / load user settings
features.notes: Settings persist engine-side as XML; every frontend loads/saves through the engine.

features.title: User-facing speed control
features.notes: Speed stepper/slider on every frontend plus optional auto-speed. Range note (Aug 2026): the engine now accepts v5's full range (raw 10–800, DasherCore v0.2.3+); Android (v0.1.7+) and GTK (v0.2.6+) follow it; Windows still caps at 5.0× (Dasher-Windows #27) and Apple at 4.0× (Dasher-Apple #34).

features.title: Button / key remapping
features.notes: Apple supports switch key capture (4 profiles). GTK supports live key recording. Android/Windows not yet.

features.title: Live mini-canvas preview in settings
features.notes: A mini Dasher canvas inside the settings window previewing changes live.

features.title: Multiple UI languages
features.notes: Engine strings localised (33 locale files); UI chrome localisation is progressing platform by platform. GTK auto-selects the engine locale from the system language.

macos.reason: Engine strings localised; chrome still English

ios.reason: Engine strings localised; chrome still English

visionos.reason: Engine strings localised; chrome still English

windows.reason: Engine strings localised; chrome still English

features.title: Guided first-run onboarding
features.notes: First-run welcome, input handshake and first-zoom tutorial.

features.title: Gamified training (Game Mode)
features.notes: Target text with correct/wrong/remaining tracking and a help path. Apple fully wired with custom text; Windows wired (target bar + game WPM); Android in beta; GTK's button is still not connected.

features.title: Custom game / training text files
features.notes: Load your own text as the Game Mode target.

features.title: iOS system keyboard extension
features.notes: Keyboard extension sharing settings with the main app via an app group (RFC 0008 covers enablement onboarding — not yet implemented).

android.reason: Android uses the IME; see direct-text-injection

features.title: visionOS app
features.notes: Dasher for visionOS: native eye gaze + pinch + dwell indicator.

features.title: Shared settings (app & keyboard)
features.notes: Apple: app group shared between app and keyboard extension. Android: the IME shares filesDir with the main app.

features.title: Privacy-preserving analytics & crash reporting
features.notes: Opt-in analytics + crash reporting via self-hosted PostHog (RFC 0001) with scrubbed engine-log tails (RFC 0009). No text content ever collected. Shipped on Windows, Apple, GTK (v0.2.6+) and Android.

visionos.reason: SDK linked; opt-in prompt not yet shown

features.title: Lucide icon set
features.notes: Unified cross-platform icon library (RFC 0002). Android deliberately stays on Material Symbols.

features.title: v5 to v6 settings migration
features.notes: One-shot opt-in import of v5 settings, custom alphabets/colours/control trees and training files. Shipped on Windows and macOS; GTK pending (the XML format matches, so much can be shared).

ios.reason: No v5 iOS app to migrate from

visionos.reason: No v5 visionOS app to migrate from

android.reason: No v5 Android app in this lineage
